headline: AI agent self-improvement found only noise in 58 configurations
summary: A year-long project building a meta-loop for self-improving AI agents concluded that all tested configurations failed to show improvement over the base model.
details: A developer spent a year building ALMA, a governance layer for self-improving AI agents. The system included a meta-loop that proposed changes to itself, a validator it could not edit, pre-registered experiments, and a claim ledger.

The meta-loop repeatedly identified potential 'improvements.' However, rigorous measurement using larger selection panels, a recalibrated adoption threshold, and split-half diagnosis revealed that the 'positives' were merely selected noise. In 7 out of 7 reversed tests, the improvements failed on held-out data.

With the chosen panel size, approximately 65 replicates would have been needed to statistically certify the perceived effect. After re-measuring all 58 configurations against this new, stricter standard, none outperformed the base model. The meta-loop recorded zero lifetime adoptions.

Instead of tuning until a favorable result emerged, the developer closed the search and published the null result as a certified finding. The code repository is publicly available, featuring all test suites and a green CI status, along with the full delta (δ) arc and the diagnosis that halted the search.

The next phase involves an external judge. The project's reviewer has been approved on ReviewBench, a benchmark for code-review agents. When scored runs are completed, each will include a manifest detailing the exact container image digest, model, configuration, the specific differing field, and the judge's verbatim result to ensure reproducibility and prevent manipulation.
caption:

headline: Apple acquires AI startup Samplab for music production tools
summary: The tech giant has purchased the Swiss company, which specializes in AI-powered music creation, signaling a potential expansion into the audio production space.
details: Apple has acquired Samplab, a Swiss startup focused on AI-driven music production. The company's technology aims to offer advanced tools for musicians in the age of artificial intelligence.

Samplab's offerings reportedly include AI-powered features that can assist in various aspects of music creation, from generating ideas to refining final tracks. This acquisition could signal Apple's intent to integrate sophisticated AI into its existing music software and hardware.

While specific details of the deal remain undisclosed, the acquisition of Samplab aligns with Apple's ongoing efforts to enhance its creative professional tools. The company has a history of acquiring smaller tech firms to bolster its product capabilities.

This move could lead to new features in applications like Logic Pro or GarageBand, potentially offering musicians more powerful and intuitive ways to create and manipulate audio using AI. Further integration could also extend to Apple's hardware, such as the Mac and iPad Pro lines.
